summary: Close the Art-Net/sACN silent-failure path by replacing the swallowing error handlers with a single reporting seam, and by deriving the send gate from live socket state rather than a ready flag set once in the bind callback.

design.title: Introduce an OutputFault sink behind the transport interface
design.intent: Both adapters currently install on('error', () => {}), so a stale interface after an ethernet-to-wifi switch fails silently. One sink behind the existing interface means the adapters gain reporting without gaining surface.
design.verification: New unit test asserts an emitted socket error reaches the sink; madge confirms packages/core still does not import packages/io.

design.title: Derive the send gate from socket state in both adapters
design.intent: Replace the bind-callback ready flag in the Art-Net and sACN adapters with a state read, so a socket that dies after bind stops reporting itself as sendable.
design.verification: Existing io suite green plus a new test that closes the socket mid-run and asserts sends stop and a fault is reported; output adapters stay fire-and-forget (no await added to the render path).
design.reverses: Revert this step's commit alone; S1's sink is additive and can stay in place with no caller.

interface_deltas.note: Two per-adapter flags collapse into one shared fault type.

checks: pnpm gates on committed HEAD, compared against the Phase 0 baseline test count
madge boundary check: packages/core reaches neither Node, DOM nor @ledrums/io
behaviour_parity_evidence_plan.known_gaps: Neither adapter's socket path is exercised against real hardware in CI, so a green suite does not prove a live PixLite still receives frames; that check is a manual bench run before the initiative is called done.

rollback_strategy: Two commits, one per step, landed in order. Reverting S2 restores the previous gate with no data or config migration; reverting S1 afterwards removes the sink. No persisted state changes, so rollback is pure git.

open_questions.question: Should a reported output fault surface in the UI as a banner, or only in the server log for this initiative?
